Hi Aditi / Samir —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our mutual action plan draft, attached is a slimmed econ appendix and the evaluation plan (LumaCare-eval-plan.xlsx) so both teams have the same inputs for token economics. Quick note on what we need from you before we lock the MAP and commit:

- Confirm expected daily active users (DAU) that will hit LLM workflows and an average prompt/response token pair (prompt tokens + expected generated tokens) by use-case. Example row in the spreadsheet.
- Any expected long-context sessions ( > 4k tokens) or multimodal assets — that materially changes the cost profile.
- Desired close date (you mentioned end of July) so we can align reserved capacity vs hosted routing assumptions.

Attached: MAP-LumaCare-v2.pdf (MAP with milestones), LumaCare-eval-plan.xlsx (test prompts + traffic shapes). Also attached a small csv with the numbers I pulled for the first-pass calc (rishi-econ-notes.csv).

A few high-level assumptions baked into the sheet so you can sanity-check quickly:
- Baseline model: redwood-llama-70b-8k-quant (serving price used = $0.00045 per token generated; prompt tokens billed same unit).
- Expected tokens per session: median 1,250 total tokens (350 prompt / 900 generation) — we flagged this as sensitive.
- Caching: we assumed a 12% prefix cache hit rate for common system prompts & templates (saves ~350 prompt tokens at hit).
- Batching: production batching yields avg effective throughput tokens/w GPU that reduces per-token cost by ~18% under our Dedicated profile at projected QPS; we model both hosted and reserved rows.

Can you confirm the DAU and any higher-context workflows by EOD Friday? If that works we’ll push a MAP update and a short joint plan to hit the July 29 close target.

If helpful, I can run a 20-minute walkthrough of the calc with your ops lead — propose Wed 23rd 10am PT.

Thanks,

Adding the econ breakdown from my side (see rishi-econ-notes.csv). Key points and sensitivity runs I recommend we include in the MAP appendix:

- Pricing rows: hosted public list used for transparency = $0.00050 / token (both prompt+generated) — Dedicated reserved effective unit (modeled) after reservation + batching = $0.00032 / token. I put both lines in the sheet so finance on their side can see tradeoffs.

- Example quick calc (pilot, daily):
  • 6,000 sessions/day * 800 tokens/session (ops midpoint) = 4,800,000 tokens/day
  • At hosted price ($0.00050) => $2,400/day => ~$72,000/month
  • At dedicated modeled price ($0.00032) => $1,536/day => ~$46,080/month

- Caching sensitivity: with a 12% cache hit (our optimistic), prompt token spend drops ~10% overall vs 5% hit (conservative) which yields ~5% total token spend reduction. I included two model runs: cache_hit=12% and cache_hit=5%.

- Batching and tail latency: we modeled batching with a median effective batch size that reduces per-token CPU/GPU time by ~18%; important note — the batching gains assume steady QPS and a 95th percentile latency SLO of 600ms. If LumaCare requires 200ms p95 we should route to lower-latency pools and adjust econ accordingly (less batching gains).

Action items I propose we put in the MAP and own:
1) LumaCare to confirm DAU and high-context feature list by Fri 6/25 (you may want 6/25 EOD).
2) Redwood to deliver 2 sensitivity runs (hosted vs dedicated) and updated MAP with explicit spend estimates by Mon 6/28.
3) Joint 30-minute walkthrough Wed 6/23 10am PT (already penciled).

I attached the csv with the three sensitivity lines and the model assumptions. If Aditi/Samir can confirm the 3k+ long-context sessions frequency (e.g., % of sessions), we can add an additional long-context cost row.

-Rishi
